# Russian strike damages Ukraine Danube port as Moscow intercepts drones

*Port infrastructure hit in southern Ukraine as drones intercepted over Russian capital.*

Save

![The port of Izmail seen from Plauru, Romania](/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/2023-09-05T173027Z_2097074460_RC2C23ADC5GD_RTRMADP_3_UKRAINE-CRISIS-ATTACK-DANUBE-ROMANIA-1694069424.jpg?resize=770%2C513&quality=80)
![](/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/2017-06-08T131939Z_1189275883_RC11B0FE7F20_RTRMADP_3_GULF-QATAR-JAZEERA-1714943623.jpg?resize=96%2C96&quality=80)

A Russian attack has damaged port infrastructure in Ukraine’s Danube River port city of Izmail, a vital grain-export hub, while Russian authorities said they had downed four Ukrainian drones headed towards Moscow, as peace efforts remain stalled and both sides continue reciprocal attacks.

Izmail, in the Odesa region, is a frequently targeted logistical centre and was hit in the early hours of Tuesday. It is Ukraine’s largest port on the Danube.

## Recommended Stories

According to the Odesa Regional State Administration, Ukrainian air defence weapons destroyed almost all the Russian UAVs over open territory outside the populated areas of the Izmail district, limiting risks to civilians. The attack lasted from about 1am to 3am (22:00 to 00:00 GMT), with firefighters battling a blaze in a building with blown-out windows.

This followed another Russian attack on port infrastructure in Izmail on the night of May 2.

# China Training Russians to Fight in Ukraine: Report

Published

updated

![Gabe Whisnant](https://assets.newsweek.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/2316314-gabe-whisnant.jpg?w=1600&quality=80&webp=1)

Breaking News Editor

[China](/topic/china)’s military secretly trained around 200 Russian soldiers in 2025, some of whom later returned to fight in [Ukraine](/topic/ukraine), according to a Reuters investigation.

The revelation raises fresh questions about [Beijing’s role in the war](https://www.newsweek.com/putin-xi-3-things-russia-wants-from-china-11963596), potentially undermining its claims of neutrality and increasing scrutiny from Western governments. The findings could heighten geopolitical tensions and influence policy responses from the U.S. and its allies as [Russia](/topic/russia)’s war in Ukraine continues.

The training, conducted under a confidential bilateral agreement signed in July 2025, included drone warfare and other modern combat tactics at Chinese military facilities, Reuters reported, citing European intelligence agencies.
